payload.title: The parent-to-dest map of kernel-dead-wire is built by a regex that needs dest= as the first keyword of add_subparsers, keyed by variable name across the whole file, with the root pair hard-coded, so an unmatched parent is dropped with no observation and a rebound or renamed root silently changes which verbs are judged
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:96-103 (ROOT_PARENT, ROOT_DEST and SUBPARSERS_DEST_RE, which needs dest as the first keyword)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:255-258 (one file-global map keyed by variable name, last match wins, seeded with the root pair)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:264-270 (a verb whose parent has no map entry is skipped; nothing records it)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:285-295 (nested is dest !== ROOT_DEST, so a renamed root turns every root verb into one subject to the silence rule)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py:894 (the real root: sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True))
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.test.ts:93-102 (the fixture's root is a function parameter named sub, the reason the constants exist)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 3: what a detector cannot read must be observable, and one fact (the root parser) has one owner
payload.notes: A group declared k = parent.add_subparsers(required=True, dest="k_command") does not match the regex, so every verb registered on k is skipped: verbsChecked drops and no finding or observation names the parent. A root declared with dest="cmd" makes every root verb 'nested', so a lone dead root verb stops being reported. The real cli.py resolves 103 of 103 add_subparsers parents today (re-counted here with the same regex), so nothing is wrong now, and no standing test asserts that every parent resolves. Close condition: Report each add_subparsers call the map cannot resolve as a named observation and make the test fail on one in the production cli.py, derive the root parser and its dest from the parser tree instead of ROOT_PARENT and ROOT_DEST, and key the map per scope; closed when a probe with dest as the second keyword yields an observation and the two constants are gone from the adapter. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
